context: A teacher and student discuss a paleo-medicine paper
purpose: Teach: 麻酔/化石/慢性/申し立て/賞賛/予期/偏っ/迄

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 論文、化石記録から麻酔の原型を探る視点、独創的ですね。
lines.en: Your paper is genuinely original—the idea of tracing anesthesia's roots through fossil records.
lines.style: Measured, attentive opening. Slight pause after the dash. Warm recognition without excess. Eyes steady on the work, not the person.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい。慢性疾患の治療法、古代の証拠も探しました。
lines.en: Yes. I also looked for evidence of chronic-illness treatments in ancient sources.
lines.style: Quiet precision. Lean forward slightly on 'also'—he's tracking his own logic, making sure she follows. Not defensive, just exact.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 申し立てがない場合の倫理、丁寧に章を立てています。
lines.en: And you've dedicated a chapter to the ethics of cases without consent. That's thoughtfully done.
lines.style: Genuine recognition building. Slight weight on 'thoughtfully.' Not perfunctory praise—she's identifying what matters in the work and naming it.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 査読者の賞賛、予期していました。
lines.en: I wasn't sure the reviewers would pick up on that.
lines.style: Quiet surprise underneath. Not quite self-doubt, more like—he built something he hoped was there but couldn't be certain. Small, honest vulnerability.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 偏った解釈を避けるため、近世迄の文献、丹念に追っていますね。
lines.en: But you traced the sources carefully all the way through to the early-modern period. That's how you avoid reading bias into it.
lines.style: Teacher-voice settling in now. Not instructing—affirming the discipline behind his choice. Slower, more reflective. Emphasis lands on the method, not the result.
